simulations.title: Simulated features
simulations.subtitle: What really works and what is simulated
simulations.intro: Editing, selection, the inspector, fades, the prompt library, the assistant, conflict checks, AI generation and takes, exports, the 3D scene (scenes built from an image, imported splats and Blender files, the camera, captures and reference videos) and the console work for real. The following are simulated and carry the {badge} badge:
simulations.identity.title: Identity score
simulations.identity.text: The identity similarity between two shots, in the continuity check and in the assistant’s review, is simulated. The color match really analyzes the images.
simulations.lipSync.title: Lip sync
simulations.lipSync.text: No lip sync is computed: the lip sync options of the Sound design workshop stay in the project and change neither the takes nor the export.
simulations.voice.title: Generated voices and dialogue
simulations.voice.text: The Sound design workshop generates no voice, dialogue or sound: preparing is simulated and what you hear is a simple synthesis in the browser. The dialogue text feeds the subtitles, and imported audio files play for real.
simulations.console.title: Console automation and processing
simulations.console.text: The Auto button only switches a mode: no automation curve is recorded. Pan, inserts, sends and the master bus are heard in the browser but are not applied to the exported video, which keeps the gain, the track faders, mute, solo and the fades.
simulations.formats.title: ProRes, H.265 and stems
simulations.formats.text: The master file (ProRes), the archive (H.265) and the audio stems are simulated: no file is written. The web and social MP4 videos and the FCPXML, OTIO, EDL and SRT files are real.
simulations.guidance.title: Guidance of the Control videos
simulations.guidance.text: The guidance strength of a Control video stays in the project but does not change the takes: the engine reads the guide video as it is.
